title: Land and Time
paragraphs: Given that the types and modes of love behaviour of the hero and the heroine and the attendant situations and sub-situations as prescribed in Tolkāppiyam are being discussed in the succeeding chapters, it is necessary to briefly introduce them here.
Pastoral tract (mullai): Season--rainy season; time of the day - evening.
Hilly tract (kuṟiñci): Season--winter; time of the day - midnight
Agricultural tract (marutam): Season--all seasons; time of the day - dawn
Maritime land (neytal): Season--all seasons; time of the day - sunset.
The desert tract, not included among the four above, has the hot summer season and the midday hour for its season and hour of the day.
> The rainy season and evening > Are assigned to the forest tract. > The learned find > The cold season and midnight hour > Assigned to the hilly tract. > > (Poruḷatikāram : Akattiṇai iyal, verse 6)
> The early dewy season > Does also go with the hilly tract, > So has it been said. > > (Poruḷatikāram : Akattiṇai iyal, verse7)
> The wee hours just before daybreak > Are assigned to the cultivable tract. > The day’s close before sunset > Belongs to the littoral tract. > > (Poruḷatikāram : Akattiṇai iyal, verse 8)
> As we see it, > The hot season and midday hour > Go with the centrally placed [arid] tract. > > (Poruḷatikāram : Akattiṇai iyal, verse 9)
> The last dewy season > Is also held to be proper to the arid tract. > > (Poruḷatikāram : Akattiṇai iyal, verse 10)
After having described all these, Tolkāppiyar shows that it is inevitable that the nature of love behaviour may change, and not the nature of land and its characteristics.

> That > Aspects of love behaviour > Assigned to a given tract > Do get mixed with those of another tract > Is no deviation unacceptable; > Yet, > No commingling is permitted among the tracts themselves, > So goes the norm by men of discernment. > > (Poruḷatikāram : Akattiṇai iyal, verse 12)
